outcome.description: You find the cargo bay half-stripped and three boarding drones still active. Their lights come on as you step in.
The log shows automated drones came online when the crew died. You burn the cargo bay's lock with a remote charge, scoop the loose containers with a tractor pass, and don't board.
The log buffer's corrupted. You can't tell what's still active inside.
You log the wreck for the next salvage license you sell to. Small finder's fee.
Three drones survived a stripped reactor. They were waiting for someone like you.
You spot three faint heat blooms inside. You target them with hull-piercing rounds from your own guns, then board to a quiet ship. The lockboxes are intact.
You can't get a clean read. Could be safe. Could be live.
You note the hulk and move on. Someone else's problem. Someone else's payday.
The data cores are intact. So are the security drones the crew set on a hair trigger before whatever happened, happened.
You spoof the signature. The drones acknowledge you as crew. You walk the ship, pull two cores, and leave clean.
Your spoof half-takes. The drones go to standby instead of friendly. You still have to go in with weapons live.
You ping the Collective's recovery channel with the coordinates. They thank you and credit you a finder's fee.
Two drones in the cargo bay come online the moment you step in. The crate behind them is what you came for.
You find two contact charges and a pressure plate. You bypass each one. The cargo lifts clean.
You miss something. A charge thumps your hull as you back out. Repairs cost. You still don't have the cargo.
You log the wreck for the smuggler network. They'll send a crew and pay you finder's.
